issues.description: play.ts is a developer scratch file committed with the patch
issues.detail: The diff modifies play.ts with console.log debugging and a local relative import path. This is scratch work, not a deliverable. It does not belong in the patch. Strip it out and resubmit. A patch that smuggles in unrelated debugging junk is unreviewable on principle.

issues.description: THREE-PATCHES: metadata refactor, file processor rewrite, and mini parent flag are jammed into one diff
issues.detail: This PR does three unrelated things: (1) reorders process() so parent runs after the processor and adds a separate parent field, (2) restructures fileProcessor anyOf output, (3) flips ZodMiniType to parent:true. When this regresses, bisect lands on a mess. Split it. The file processor change in particular has its own snapshot churn and deserves its own discussion.

issues.description: JSON.stringify used as a deep-equality primitive in a hot path
issues.detail: finalize() uses JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key]) twice to decide whether to delete properties. Key ordering is not guaranteed equal across objects built by different code paths, so this will silently fail to dedupe in real cases. Use a real structural compare, or compare by reference where the contract allows. This is the kind of shortcut that produces a bug nobody can reproduce.

issues.description: Test asserts overrideCount went from 6 to 12 with no explanation
issues.detail: The override block in finalize() lost its `if (!seen.isParent)` guard, so overrides now fire for parent schemas too. The test snapshot changed from 6 to 12 and nobody told the reader why doubling is correct. Either the old number was a bug (say so in the commit message and the test) or the new number is one (in which case stop). Numbers without rationale are how regressions land.

issues.description: fileProcessor anyOf restructure changes public output shape without justification
issues.detail: Previously each anyOf branch carried contentEncoding, format, maxLength, minLength, type. Now those are hoisted to the root and anyOf entries hold only contentMediaType. That is a user-visible JSON Schema change. It may be more correct, but it is buried inside a metadata-tracking PR with no commit-message argument for why downstream validators will accept the new shape. Separate patch, separate discussion.

issues.description: Cast `(zodSchema as any)._zod.parent` defeats the type system in the very file that just added a typed parent field
issues.detail: The Seen interface was just extended with a typed `parent?: $ZodType` field. Three lines into using it, the code reaches back through `(zodSchema as any)._zod.parent` to decide isParentRef. Either trust the field you just added (seen.parent === ref) or explain why the runtime source must be re-read. The any-cast in a type-heavy library is a smell.

review.summary: This patch is three patches in a trench coat: a metadata/$ref propagation rework in to-json-schema.ts, a public-shape change in fileProcessor, and a parent:true flip in mini. On top of that it ships a scratch play.ts with debugging console.logs. THREE-PATCHES, and the play.ts file is a REFUSE on its own. Substantively, the new finalize() logic leans on JSON.stringify for structural equality and reaches through `(zodSchema as any)._zod.parent` immediately after introducing a typed parent field — both are taste failures in a library this widely depended on. The overrideCount test doubling from 6 to 12 needs a real explanation, not a number swap. NEEDS-WORK: split the diffs, kill play.ts, replace the stringify compares, and justify the override count and file schema reshape in the commit message.
